subject: Cobalt Labs SDK + Redwood tracing integration — scope & acceptance
messages:
From: Sara Liu <sara@cobaltlabs.ai>
To: markus.klein@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-02T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Intro: Cobalt SDK + Redwood trace hooks / sandbox trial

Hi Markus,

Thanks for taking a look at this. I’m Sara (Product Partnerships) at Cobalt Labs — we build a developer SDK for embeddings + lightweight tracing that a number of ISVs wire into their inference stacks. We’ve been experimenting with Redwood’s runtime and think a lightweight trace/telemetry hook and an optional embedding shim would be a good fit for customers who need standardized prompt instrumentation across toolchains.

Attached are two short deck slides that sketch our integration approach (cobalt-sdk-integration-slides.pdf) and a one-page summary of the telemetry payloads we emit. High-level asks:
- Quick 90-min technical workshop with your infra/serving engineer to validate the hook API and security constraints
- A 2-week sandbox account (non-prod, isolated) where we can deploy the shim and run 100–200k test tokens across a few models
- Clarify acceptance criteria for telemetry fidelity and SLOs (latency overhead, sampling semantics)

We’d love to coordinate with whoever owns the runtime instrumentation. Would you be the right person to start? If not, could you point me to the engineer/PM who owns SDK/trace partner integrations?

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a suggested calendar slot if that helps.

Sara Liu
Product Partnerships | Cobalt Labs
https://cobaltlabs.ai

Attachment: cobalt-sdk-integration-slides.pdf (12 pages, PDF)
From: markus.klein@redwood.com
To: Sara Liu <sara@cobaltlabs.ai>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-03T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro: Cobalt SDK + Redwood trace hooks / sandbox trial

Sara — thanks for the clear notes and the deck. Happy to take this on.

Couple of quick clarifications before we schedule the tech workshop:
1) Sandbox access model: we prefer to provision a dedicated Dedicated-style sandbox project (VPC-peered) for partner integrations so we can control network egress and workload isolation. Is that acceptable?
2) Telemetry payloads: we prioritize minimal per-token overhead. Can you confirm typical payload sizes (compressed) and sampling defaults? Also we need to ensure PII is never sent — will your SDK support client-side redaction hooks?
3) Trace join keys: to link SDK traces with Redwood request ids we’ll need a stable correlation header (x-redwood-trace-id or similar). Are you open to adding that to the shim?

Looping in Marissa (Platform PM) — Marissa, Vanessa (Partner Eng) — can you own the acceptance checklist and drive the workshop schedule? Suggested attendees for the 90-min session: one runtime engineer (perf), one security engineer, partner eng, and the Cobalt SDK lead.

If that sounds good, Sara — propose Wed 10/06 or Thu 10/07 for the workshop (PST). I’ll ask Vanessa to coordinate calendar details.

Cheers,
Markus Klein
Director, Serving Integrations | Redwood Inference
From: marissa.cole@redwood.com
To: markus.klein@redwood.com, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: Sara Liu <sara@cobaltlabs.ai>
Date: 2026-10-03T17:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro: Cobalt SDK + Redwood trace hooks / sandbox trial

Thanks for the ping — happy to lead acceptance. A few items I’ll own and want to confirm with Cobalt ahead of the workshop so we have a focused agenda:

Acceptance checklist (draft):
- Provision: isolated sandbox project with RBAC and egress controls (no external DB writes)
- Perf: end-to-end p99 added latency <= 15ms for small gen requests; sample test harness attached to reproduce
- Telemetry fidelity: event-level timestamps, token counts, prompt/response hashes (not full prompt text), and stable correlation id support
- Security: client-side redaction option + proof of local-only redaction. We will run a quick SAST scan on the shim package.
- Logging & retention: partner telemetry must support configurable retention and a means to purge test data on request

For the workshop agenda I propose:
1) 15m intro & integration overview (Cobalt)
2) 30m runtime hooks & latency characteristics (Redwood infra + Cobalt SDK lead)
3) 20m security & redaction walk-through (security engineer + Cobalt lead)
4) 20m sandbox test plan + next steps (Marissa / Vanessa)

Vanessa — can you propose two 90-min slots (10/06 or 10/07 PST) and we’ll lock one. Also I attached a small test harness snippet we use to measure p99 overhead as a plain text file (we’ll share in the Drive folder).

Marissa Cole
Group PM, Platform Integrations | Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood-test-harness-snippet.txt (1 KB)
From: Sara Liu <sara@cobaltlabs.ai>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, markus.klein@redwood.com
Cc: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com, Tom Lin <tom.lin@cobaltlabs.ai>
Date: 2026-10-04T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro: Cobalt SDK + Redwood trace hooks / sandbox trial

Hi Marissa / Markus / Vanessa — great checklist, thanks. Quick responses inline and next steps: 

- Sandbox model: yes, a VPC-peered dedicated sandbox works for us. We can operate entirely within that boundary.
- Payloads: our typical compressed telemetry payload is ~180–350 bytes per event (depends on sampling). We default to 10% sampling in the SDK but can switch to 100% for short test runs.
- Redaction: SDK supports client-side redaction hooks and we can add a strict-mode config to drop any free-text fields by default; we’ll include docs + tests for proof.
- Correlation header: we’ll add support for x-redwood-trace-id; expect a minor patch to the shim.

Attached is a first-pass SOW draft (cobalt-sow-draft.docx) that outlines scope, timeline, and a proposed co-op budget for shared test infra. We’re happy to run the workshop Wed 10/06 10:00–11:30 PST — Tom (SDK lead) and I will be there.

Proposed next steps:
1) Vanessa to send calendar invite for Wed 10/06 10:00–11:30 PST
2) Redwood to provision VPC-peered sandbox by 10/08
3) Cobalt to land the correlation header patch and share a test shim release candidate by 10/09
4) Run 2-week test sweep (10/10–10/24) and review telemetry fidelity + perf metrics

We’ve uploaded the SOW and an npm package snapshot to the Drive link you provided. Let me know if you want any edits to the SOW before the meeting.

Thanks — looking forward to the workshop.

—Sara
Sara Liu
Product Partnerships | Cobalt Labs
Attachments: cobalt-sow-draft.docx (Word), npm-snapshot.tar.gz (attachment stub)
